title: 2024 HMMT February Guts Problem 7
statement: Positive integers \(a, b\), and \(c\) have the property that \(a^{b}, b^{c}\), and \(c^{a}\) end in 4,2 , and 9 , respectively. Compute the minimum possible value of \(a+b+c\).

solutions.text: This minimum is attained when \((a, b, c)=(2,2,13)\). To show that we cannot do better, observe that \(a\) must be even, so \(c\) ends in 3 or 7 . If \(c \geq 13\), since \(a\) and \(b\) are even, it's clear \((2,2,13)\) is optimal. Otherwise, \(c=3\) or \(c=7\), in which case \(b^{c}\) can end in 2 only when \(b\) ends in 8 . However, no eighth power ends in 4 , so we would need \(b \geq 18\) (and \(a \geq 2\) ), which makes the sum \(2+18+3=23\) larger than 17 .
